classification.difficultyReason: Decompose the solid into a cylinder and hemisphere, add their volumes, and select only exposed surfaces, excluding the shared circle while retaining the bottom face.

content.prompt: Find the volume and surface area of the figure shown below:

spec.description: Unfilled hemisphere on a cylinder, retaining the circular junction, bottom face, radius label and cylinder-height label. Decorative orange fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Hemisphere and cylinder share radius 2 cm; cylinder height is 2 cm. Their common circular interface is internal.

answer.short:
$V=\dfrac{40\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^3$, $A=20\pi\text{ cm}^2$.

Exclude the internal circular interface from the surface area.
answer.worked:
Add the cylinder and hemisphere volumes.
$$\begin{align*}V&=\pi r^2h+\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3\\V&=\pi(2)^2(2)+\frac{2}{3}\pi(2)^3\\V&=\frac{40\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$
The exposed surfaces are the hemisphere's curved surface, the cylinder's curved surface and the bottom circular face.
$$\begin{align*}A&=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh+\pi r^2\\A&=2\pi(2)^2+2\pi(2)(2)+\pi(2)^2\\A&=20\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
